# zupgtr

> Generates a complex unitary matrix Q which is defined as the product of.

<section class="intro">

N-1 elementary reflectors of order N, as returned by ZHPTRD using
packed storage.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zupgtr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zupgtr';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zupgtr( order, uplo, N, AP, TAU, strideTAU, Q, LDQ, WORK ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the upper or lower triangle was used in ZHPTRD ('upper' or 'lower') |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix Q<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `AP` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | Packed reflector vectors from ZHPTRD |
| `TAU` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | Scalar factors of the reflectors from ZHPTRD (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | Stride length for `TAU` |
| `Q` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output unitary matrix (N x N) |
| ↳ `LDQ` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Q`<br>Requires `LDQ ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ N - 1</sub> | **out** · Workspace array (length >= N-1) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular packed storage used in previous call to ZHPTRD;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular packed storage used in previous call to ZHPTRD.
- `N`: The order of the matrix Q. $N \ge 0$.
- `AP`: The vectors which define the elementary reflectors, as returned by ZHPTRD.
- `TAU`: `TAU(i)` must contain the scalar factor of the elementary reflector H(i), as returned by ZHPTRD.
- `Q`: The N-by-N unitary matrix Q.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zupgtr.ndarray(
    uplo,
    N,
    AP, strideAP, offsetAP,
    TAU, strideTAU, offsetTAU,
    Q, strideQ1, strideQ2, offsetQ,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Generates an orthogonal matrix Q which is defined as the product of n-1 elementary reflectors of order n, as returned by zhptrd.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'lower'`, `'upper'`. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `AP` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | Input array |
| ↳ `strideAP` | `integer` | Stride length for `AP` |
| ↳ `offsetAP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `AP` |
| `TAU` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | Input array |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | Stride length for `TAU` |
| ↳ `offsetTAU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `TAU` |
| `Q` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideQ1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `Q` |
| ↳ `strideQ2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `Q` |
| ↳ `offsetQ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `Q` |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length ≥ N - 1</sub> | **out** · Output array |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular packed storage used in previous call to ZHPTRD;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular packed storage used in previous call to ZHPTRD.
- `N`: The order of the matrix Q. $N \ge 0$.
- `AP`: The vectors which define the elementary reflectors, as returned by ZHPTRD.
- `TAU`: `TAU(i)` must contain the scalar factor of the elementary reflector H(i), as returned by ZHPTRD.
- `Q`: The N-by-N unitary matrix Q.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import zhptrd from '../zhptrd/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zupgtr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zupgtr';

// 3x3 Hermitian upper packed:
const N = 3;
const AP = new Complex128Array([
	3,
	0,
	1,
	-1,
	2,
	0,
	0,
	0,
	1,
	-1,
	1,
	0
]);
const d = new Float64Array( N );
const e = new Float64Array( N - 1 );
const TAU = new Complex128Array( N - 1 );

zhptrd( 'column-major', 'upper', N, AP, d, 1, e, 1, TAU, 1 );

const Q = new Complex128Array( N * N );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( N );

zupgtr( 'column-major', 'upper', N, AP, TAU, 1, Q, N, WORK );

console.log( 'Unitary matrix Q:', reinterpret( Q, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZUPGTR`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZUPGTR generates a complex unitary matrix Q which is defined as the product of n-1 elementary reflectors H(i) of order n, as returned by ZHPTRD using packed storage:

if `UPLO = 'U'`, $Q = H(n-1)$ . . . H(2) H(1),

if `UPLO = 'L'`, $Q = H(1)$ H(2) . . . H(n-1).

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
